Subject: Major latency spikes during morning scale events

Hi Stephanie —

We hit multiple production incidents this morning between 08:45–09:30 ET where our p95 and p99 latencies jumped dramatically (p95 from ~120ms to ~2.4s, p99 to ~6.8s) when your Hosted API autoscaled GPUs. Error rate also rose from ~0.3% to ~3.7% for a 20-minute window. This coincided with an increase in tail latencies for model generate calls. Our infra team saw warmup spikes on the first token during scale-outs.

This is impacting our batch jobs and interactive products — we need an urgent explanation and mitigation. Can Redwood confirm whether this is related to the new autoscale policy that spun up N+2 pools?

Attached: sample request IDs and timestamps.

— Elena

Subject: Re: Fwd: EverStore - latency spikes during autoscale (initial triage)

Quick triage notes (initial):
- We reproduced the tail spike locally against the same quantized variant with autoscale enabled. The p95 jump aligns with GPU allocation + offload initialization and KV cache population for long-context prompts.
- Root causes likely combined: (1) container cold-start + shared library JIT compilation paths, (2) synchronous KV-cache repopulation on first few requests, and (3) our autoscaler launching multiple replicas simultaneously (thundering-spinup) which creates concurrent initialization pressure on local host and storage layers.
- Error-rate bump tracked to 503s from upstream timeouts when the Nginx proxy backlog exceeded backlog_limit during bursty spin-ups.

Immediate mitigations we can roll out (short term):
- Increase warm pool target for EverStore by +2 GPUs for 24–48h (fast).
- Stagger replica spin-up (introduce 6s jitter) to avoid simultaneous JIT hit.
- Add lightweight async KV-cache prefetch on container start to make first-request lighter.

I'll attach a filtered set of traces (trace-logs-20270412.txt) showing kernel init times and first-token latencies. Follow-up plan: deeper profiling of JIT path and possible precompiled kernels for this quantized model.

— Rishi
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
